question: Can a smallest family symmetry on three families relate Y_PP and Y_PN in the shared Spin(10) 126 tensor while preserving the Dirac null mask and Majorana P-N sewing?

requiredSectorData.sectorDistinction: the same family P-N label is forbidden on Dirac support and required on Majorana support

universalShared126NoGo.assumption: one family matrix Y_126 multiplies both the (15,2,2) Dirac branch and the (10,1,3) Majorana branch, with nonzero branch VEV/Clebsch factors v_D and v_M
universalShared126NoGo.contradiction: D_PN=0 and M_PN nonzero cannot both hold when v_D and v_M are nonzero
universalShared126NoGo.strength: independent of which family symmetry fixes Y_126
universalShared126NoGo.conclusion: A single universal shared-126 family tensor cannot preserve the sector-dependent null mask.

permutationAudit.structuralInvariant: Congruence by a family permutation preserves equality pattern of index pairs: diagonal entries map only to diagonal entries and off-diagonal entries only to off-diagonal entries.
permutationAudit.consequence: PP and PN are in different orbits for every permutation subgroup, so no permutation symmetry can relate them nontrivially.

fixedDimensions.texture: one common diagonal plus one common off-diagonal
one common diagonal plus one common off-diagonal

maskFailures: P<->N equates PP with NN, so nonzero PP activates forbidden NN
I<->N equates PI with PN, so nonzero PN activates the forbidden Dirac PI entry
C3 or S3 makes all off-diagonals equal and all diagonals equal, activating forbidden entries

signedPermutationAudit.structuralInvariant: Signed monomial congruence still preserves diagonal and off-diagonal coordinate subspaces.
signedPermutationAudit.consequence: No signed-permutation subgroup has an orbit containing both PP and PN. If both fixed sectors are nonzero, their amplitudes remain at least two independent invariant parameters.

examples.effect: keeps PP and PN but leaves them independent while killing PI and IN
keeps only diagonal entries and therefore kills the needed PN portal

u1CharacterAudit.selectionBoundary: A U(1) can permit or forbid entries but never equates their coefficients. Keeping both PP and PN also gives P and N the same character, so the U(1) cannot preserve their marked distinction or distinguish Dirac P-N from Majorana P-N.

rankOneAudit.maskConflict: the required Majorana complementary-null entry Y_NN=0 is activated

markedSplitStabilizerAudit.fullFlagStabilizer: U(1)_P x U(1)_I x U(1)_N, or its finite monomial subgroups
markedSplitStabilizerAudit.moduleDecomposition: Sym2(F)=Sym2(P) direct-sum (P tensor Q) direct-sum Sym2(Q), of dimensions 1+2+3
markedSplitStabilizerAudit.homResult: PP lies in Sym2(P), while PN lies in P tensor Q; no intertwiner exists under the natural stabilizer.
markedSplitStabilizerAudit.boundary: Any family rotation that mixes PP with PN must mix the marked P and N lines and therefore moves the null projector and its sector anchors.

coefficientProjectorAudit.status: A rank-one projector in the six-dimensional coefficient space can select this line, but it explicitly contains the desired tensor and is not induced by a family permutation, character symmetry, or rank-one family vector.
coefficientProjectorAudit.universalTensorFailure: Used as one Y_126, it still activates Dirac P-N and therefore fails the sector mask.

properties: D_PP and M_PN share one coefficient
the heavy Majorana matrix is invertible
minimalSectorDependentConstruction.cost: requires a sector-labelled intertwiner/projector distinguishing the Dirac and Majorana 126 branches; this is not one universal Spin(10) Yukawa matrix and therefore breaks or extends the naive shared-126 parent relation

strongestNoGo: Within compact family symmetries generated by permutations, signed permutations, U(1) characters, rank-one family projectors, or the natural stabilizer of the marked P/I/N split, no one-dimensional invariant portal ray relates nonzero PP and PN while preserving the null mask. More strongly, one universal Y_126 cannot make its PN entry vanish in the Dirac branch and survive in the Majorana branch.
reopeningDatum: Supply a sector-dependent family tensor or natural transformation Xi in (Dirac/Majorana branch labels) tensor Sym2(F*) whose two components are proportional to E_PP and sym(PN), and derive Xi from an enlarged parent representation or finite-geometry anchor rather than inserting it. Then prove compatibility with Spin(10) breaking, J/CP, anomaly-free family gauging, threshold normalization and RG stability.
verdict: The shared-126 route cannot preserve the programme's null mask with one universal family Yukawa matrix. Standard three-family symmetries cannot relate a diagonal entry PP to an off-diagonal entry PN without either leaving two parameters or activating forbidden entries. The smallest algebraically viable texture uses one common coefficient in two sector-dependent tensors, so the next datum is a branch-labelled family intertwiner, not an ordinary family symmetry.
